title: Graph neural networks identify oxides for hydrogen production
summary: A model of oxygen-vacancy properties selected twelve oxides to test for thermochemical hydrogen production; about 80% were active in experiments. Some were comparable to or better than the baseline only under certain reactor conditions; further study and optimization are needed.
ai_technology: Graph neural networks for crystal defects
organization: Sandia National Laboratories and HydroGEN collaborators

evidence.tested: Twelve metal oxides selected by the model for oxygen-vacancy properties were tested experimentally for thermochemical hydrogen production; about 80% were effective, and some matched or beat the state-of-the-art material only under certain reactor conditions.
evidence.unknown: The method so far covers only thermochemical hydrogen materials, the model needs more diverse training data and more precise calculations, and the page gives no baseline numbers.
evidence.ai_role: A graph neural network trained on first-principles calculations predicted oxygen-vacancy formation energies and screened materials from existing databases.
